title: What if COD zombies were eggs instead, new game launch!
author: rectangle_so
selftext:
I'm building [EggVerse.co](http://EggVerse.co) an arcade centered around these cute eggs in all sorts of different environment/games.

For this one I thought, what if spoiled eggs were zombies, and when the egg cracked when it took damage andddd then it kind of spiraled from there.

So here's the newest game for the eggverse - Spoiled Egg its a wave-based zombie shooter, basically COD Zombies but with walking eggs instead of people. 

You grab kitchen weapons from the spoiled eggs you crack (whisk blaster, hand mixer, fork launcher)

Here is how I made it

* Claude did a lot of the heavy lifting, and the underlying game was built with TypeScript on a custom HTML5 canvas engine.
* Chat generated the game assets, 
* I drew & designed the egg characters myself, and worked with a pixel artist years ago when I made my first game "Egg on the Run", I made 11 character sprites and the rest of the new art (zombie eggs, scenery, weapons etc) was generated using descriptive prompts I wrote to match the illustrative pixel-art style using Codex.
* The part I struggled with the most was making it actually feel smooth on both desktop & mobile. Desktop was easy wherever your mouse is, you could shoot in that direction pressing space or clicking. On mobile I originally just had a shoot button & I was like okay... this is not smooth nor does it feel natural. So I ended up making two joysticks, one for moving & one for aiming/shooting and honestly it worked out great.

Curious how other people building games handle mobile + desktop controls?

Spoiled Egg is live now for free @ [eggverse.co](http://eggverse.co/)
